# Load coastal shapefile and define projection

```{r, ROMS.test}

# Since the data falls within two UTM zones and there is not an ideal projection to use, apply a custom equal area Albers projection
aea_custom <- "+proj=aea +lat_1=30 +lat_2=50 +lat_0=40 +lon_0=-124.5 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"

# High res coastal boundary from NOAA
land.barrier <- read_sf(here(dir, "Data", "Shapefiles", "land.barrier.shp"))

# Load YearSeason gaps to fill
load(file = here(dir, "Data", "ExampleRun",
                                    "est.missing.time2.rda"))

```

# Load YearSeason data (with MLD) and calculate density

Note you will need to redefine the transect centres to get X and Y and that you need to adjust the data depending on whether a fixed 30m or mld is used.

```{r, load.seasonal.data.mld}

# Load new sdm data
TwoSeas.dat <- fread(here(dir, "Data", 
                           "mld.final_table_allHistoric.csv"))

# Boxplot to check for "Empty" combinations and outliers
FulldatLengthbinObs <-
  ggplot(TwoSeas.dat %>%
         filter(len.bin != "" & 
                  !Year %in% c(2009:2011) &
                  Year < 2021 & 
                  Season == "Summer"), 
       aes(x = as.factor(YearSeas), y = Bin_Haul_Biomass, fill = len.bin)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_y_log10() + # Weights are usually log-normal
  facet_wrap(~len.bin, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Sardine Weight Distribution",
       x = "Year/Season", 
       y = "Total Weight (Log Scale)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))

FulldatLengthbinObs

ggsave2(filename="FulldatLengthbinObsByYearBoxplot.jpeg",
        plot=FulldatLengthbinObs, device="jpeg", 
        path=here(dir, "Final.Figures",
                  "S2.length.bin.exploration"),
        dpi=1200, width = 29, height=21, 
        unit="cm", limitsize = FALSE)

```

Note without having lengths per year the model cannot run. Trying random year effects
also fail when using iid and no extra time argument.

# Create transect data

```{r, create.transect.data}

survey.transects.st <- TwoSeas.dat %>%
  select(keys, Year, len.bin, lenBin.nb, Bin_Haul_Biomass, Season, 
         Fin_sweep.m3, latBin, YearSeas, YearSeas.nm, mean_depth,
         start_latitude, start_longitude, stop_latitude, 
         stop_longitude, Country, Species_weight) %>%
  # Remove absence data
  filter(len.bin != "")

# Create a tibble

# 1. Initialize an empty list (NOT a vector or table)
results_list <- list()

for(k in unique(survey.transects.st$keys)){
  
  # Use key-based subsetting
  ori.dat = survey.transects.st[keys == k]
  
  # Create your fill data
  fill.dat = data.table(
    keys = rep(ori.dat$keys, 3), 
    Year = rep(ori.dat$Year, 3),
    len.bin = c("200+", "150to200", "less150"),
    Bin_Haul_Biomass = 0, # data.table automatically repeats single values
    lenBin.nb = 0, # data.table automatically repeats single values
    Season = rep(ori.dat$Season, 3),
    Fin_sweep.m3 = rep(ori.dat$Fin_sweep.m3, 3),
    latBin = rep(ori.dat$latBin, 3), # Note: corrected from ori.dat$Fin_sweep.m3
    YearSeas = rep(ori.dat$YearSeas, 3),
    YearSeas.nm = rep(ori.dat$YearSeas.nm, 3),
    mean_depth = rep(ori.dat$mean_depth, 3),
    start_latitude = rep(ori.dat$start_latitude, 3),
    start_longitude = rep(ori.dat$start_longitude, 3),
    stop_latitude = rep(ori.dat$stop_latitude, 3), 
    stop_longitude = rep(ori.dat$stop_longitude, 3),
    Country = rep(ori.dat$Country, 3), 
    Species_weight = rep(ori.dat$Species_weight, 3)
  )
  
  # 2. Store the iteration result in the list
  # We combine ori and fill for this specific key
  results_list[[k]] <- rbind(ori.dat, fill.dat)
}

# 3. Join everything together at once
new.dat <- rbindlist(results_list)
  
new.dat.sum <- new.dat %>%
  group_by(keys, Year, Season, Fin_sweep.m3, len.bin, latBin, YearSeas, 
           YearSeas.nm, mean_depth, start_latitude, start_longitude, 
           stop_latitude, stop_longitude, Country, Species_weight) %>%
  summarise(Species_weight = first(Species_weight),
            Bin_Haul_Biomass = sum(Bin_Haul_Biomass),
            lenBin.nb = sum(lenBin.nb),
            .groups = "keep") %>%
  ungroup()
# View(new.dat.sum)  
  
final.dat <- new.dat.sum %>%
  mutate(FID = keys,
         # Set length bin as factor
         len.bin = as.factor(len.bin)
         )
# View(final.dat)

# Note data will be in wgs84
survey.transects3.sf <- 
  make_transect_sf(final.dat, crs = 4326) 

survey.transects3.sf.clip <- survey.transects3.sf %>%
  mutate(X = st_coordinates(st_centroid(.))[,1],
         Y = st_coordinates(st_centroid(.))[,2]) %>%
  filter(Y < 52)

range(survey.transects3.sf.clip$Y)
# [1] 31.5053  50.6905

## Create X Y columns and extract polygon centers
TwoSeas.dat4 <- survey.transects3.sf.clip %>%
  # Project the data to Albers Conical Equal Area
  st_transform(., crs = aea_custom) %>%
  # Extract the centre of the transect (this is in km)
  mutate(X = st_coordinates(st_centroid(.))[,1]/1000,
         Y = st_coordinates(st_centroid(.))[,2]/1000) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() 

range(TwoSeas.dat4$X)
# [1] -308.2030  668.1958

range(TwoSeas.dat4$Y)
# [1] -946.052  1206.229

```

## For Season 2 define spatial boundaries

```{r, sptl.boundaries2}

# Filter the data frame
Season.2.dat <- TwoSeas.dat4 %>%
  filter(Season == "Summer" & !Year %in% c(2009:2011) &
           # To be able to compare with ROMS
           Year < 2021
         ) 

# Delineate spatial domain
Season.2.dat <- 
  Season.2.dat[Season.2.dat$X >= min(Season.2.dat$X) & 
                 Season.2.dat$X <= max(Season.2.dat$X) & 
                 Season.2.dat$Y >= min(Season.2.dat$Y) & 
                 Season.2.dat$Y <= max(Season.2.dat$Y), ]

# Function to test for values ending in .1
integerFunction <- function(x) {
  abs(x %% 1 - 0.1) < 1e-8
}

vals <- integerFunction(est.missing.time2) 

# Apply the function to filter values ending in .1
est.missing.time.S2 <- est.missing.time2[vals]
est.missing.time.S2
# [1] 2009.1 2010.1 2011.1 2020.1

```

# Group like gear configurations

This is based on the literature and survey reports across the US and Canadian Survey segments. Each group used the same gear configuration and overall strategy, but may have more samples in some years than others. The general gear opening dimensions are also comparable within each group.

```{r, gear.configs}

Season.2.dat <- Season.2.dat %>%
  mutate(GearConfig = case_when(
    Country == "Canada" & Year < 2017 ~ "CADpre2017",
    Country == "Canada" & Year == 2017 ~ "CAD2017",
    Country == "Canada" & Year > 2017 ~ "CADpost2017",
    Country == "USA" & Year < 2011 ~ "USApre2011",
    Country == "USA" & Year >= 2011 & Year < 2015 ~ "USA2011-2014",
    Country == "USA" & Year >= 2015 & Year < 2020 ~ "USApost2014"
  ))

```

# Define offset

```{r, gear.configs}

Season.2.dat <- Season.2.dat %>%
  mutate(LogArea = log(Fin_sweep.m3),
         LogAreaMLD = log(Fin_sweep.m3*mean_depth),
         FID = as.factor(FID)
  )

```

# Define study plan

General Steps:

Step 1: The Foundation (Mesh & Barrier)

- Because the base model without regard to length bin used a barrier mesh and 37.5 km minimum distance between nodes, as long at the matérn range is appropriate we will keep these assumptions here. If your Range is significantly larger than your 37.5 km cutoff (ideally the range should be at least 2–3x the cutoff), your mesh is fine. 

Step 2: The Error Structure (Distribution)

- Goal: Find which family (Gamma, Tweedie, LogNormal, etc.) best handles the positive catch only.
- Method: Use the winner from Step 1 and the same Stratified Folds if available.
- Note: Positive catches account for only 13% of the data and it may not be possible to use cross fold validation.

Step 3: The Ecological Signal (Covariates)

- Goal: Determine which environmental variables (temp, depth, etc.) actually improve predictions.
- Method: Use the winner from Step 1 & 2 and the same Stratified Folds.
- Selection: Use ELPD to see if adding a covariate actually adds "information" or just "noise."

Step 4: The Robustness Check (Sensitivity Analysis)

- Goal: Prove your results aren't just a fluke of the fold method.
- Method: Take your Final "Best" Model and run it through Spatial Block Folds or Random Folds.
- What you are looking for: If the model performs well in Stratified but terrible in Spatial Blocks, it means your model is good at "filling in gaps" but bad at "extrapolating." If it performs well in both, you have a very powerful, generalizable model.

# Create folds (this is your most restrictive method)

Note that latBins was chosen based on the general survey sampling designs and the annual catch weight distributions across the 5 areas. The distributions were very similar for for the CalCOFI region so these were grouped together.

Originally we combined like-gears and spatial area to ensure that the unique combinations of gear and location. But because we have so few samples when we exclude the absence data, instead of splitting the data across folds (which sometimes returns only 1 or 2 observations), we need to try another approach. 

Here we use Leave-One-Group-Out (LOGO) based on Strata Identity.
We first look at how many groups we have for combined like-gears and spatial area,
Then by spatial area only, and lastly by like-gears only.

We compare this against the strata k-fold cross validation.

```{r, test.folds}

# Check the distribution of your strata
## Note without absence data we are significantly restricted
Season.2.dat %>%
  count(GearConfig, latBin) %>%
  filter(n < 10) # Any results here will be missing from at least one fold

# Check the distribution of your strata
## Note without absence data we are significantly restricted
Season.2.dat %>%
  count(latBin) %>%
  filter(n < 10) # Any results here will be missing from at least one fold

# Check the distribution of your strata
## Note without absence data we are significantly restricted
Season.2.dat %>%
  count(GearConfig) %>%
  filter(n < 10) # Any results here will be missing from at least one fold

# We 'force' the folds to respect the the spatial areas only
Season.2.dat <- Season.2.dat %>%
  # 'drop = TRUE' removes combinations that don't exist in your data
  ## But it is not needed here
  mutate(fold_idx = as.integer(as.factor(latBin))
  )

# Verify how many unique folds you just created
n_folds <- max(Season.2.dat$fold_idx)
print(n_folds)
# [1] 4

latbin.sampFolds <- Season.2.dat %>% group_by(fold_idx) %>% summarise(n = n()) 
latbin.sampFolds
# 1   204
# 2   597
# 3   147
# 4   231

#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Note that if the cross validation fails with the LOGO approach,
# You will need to use that strata cross validation
#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Season.2.dat.w.folds.is.made = F

if (Season.2.dat.w.folds.is.made == F){
  
  set.seed(123) # Lock the shuffle
  # We 'force' the folds to respect the gear/bin combinations
  Season.2.dat.w.folds <- Season.2.dat %>%
    groupdata2::fold(
      k = 5, 
      cat_col = c("GearConfig", "latBin")
      )

  # SAVE THIS DATASET NOW!!!
  ## While it is good practice to set.seed before cross validation,
  ## this is the step where that will cause the starting value to change.
  saveRDS(Season.2.dat.w.folds, "Season.2.NegBionom2.3-LengethBin.test.w.folds.rds")

}

dim(Season.2.dat.w.folds)
# [1] 1179  25

sort(unique(Season.2.dat.w.folds$.folds))
# [1] 1 2 3 4 5
# Levels: 1 2 3 4 5

sampFolds <- Season.2.dat.w.folds %>% group_by(.folds) %>% summarise(n = n()) 
sampFolds
# 1	233			
# 2	237			
# 3	234			
# 4	237			
# 5	238	

```

# Load Barrier Mesh (without MLD) at 42.5 km minimum distance

Note this is from the full data base model output.

```{r, load.barrier.mesh.mld.37.5km.dist}

# 1. Load your "Full" mesh object (the one you saved)
barrier2mld_42.5 <- readRDS(
  file = here(dir, "Final.Results",
              "barrier2mld_42.5.rds"))

## If greater than >1,000–2,000 nodes, 
## you’re likely in trouble unless you have a lot of RAM.
length(barrier2mld_42.5$mesh$loc[,1])
# [1] 176

# Example plot code from ?add_barrier_mesh
mesh_df_water_mld_42.5 <- 
  barrier2mld_42.5$mesh_sf[barrier2mld_42.5$normal_triangles, ]
mesh_df_land_mld_42.5 <- 
  barrier2mld_42.5$mesh_sf[barrier2mld_42.5$barrier_triangles, ]

Mesh.with.barrier_mld_42.5 <-
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = land.barrier) +
  geom_sf(data = mesh_df_water_mld_42.5, size = 1, colour = "blue") +
  geom_sf(data = mesh_df_land_mld_42.5, size = 1, colour = "green")

Mesh.with.barrier_mld_42.5

# 2.1 Update it with only total catch (Season.2.dat.w.folds)
# for full.dat 
Season.2.dat.w.folds.full <- Season.2.dat.w.folds %>% 
  select(-c(len.bin, Bin_Haul_Biomass)) %>%
  mutate(lenBin.nb = sum(lenBin.nb)) %>%
  distinct() 

# 2.2 Create barrier
nolength_mesh <- sdmTMB::make_mesh(
  data = Season.2.dat.w.folds.full, 
  xy_cols = c("X", "Y"), 
  mesh = barrier2mld_42.5$mesh # This "borrows" the physical structure of the old mesh
)

# 3. Update it for your Length Bin data (Season.2.dat.w.folds)
length_mesh <- sdmTMB::make_mesh(
  data = Season.2.dat.w.folds, 
  xy_cols = c("X", "Y"), 
  mesh = barrier2mld_42.5$mesh # This "borrows" the physical structure of the old mesh
)

```

# Compare model componets with Presence only

Because we cannot use a hurdle model for length bin distributions, we need to 
run the model again using only presence data. This is not meant to replace the 
best fit model but to allow for the assessment of including length bin under 
the positive catch component of the model.

## For full data

Taking the total catch (excluding absence hauls), identify the best fit model.

### Negative binomial with REML (year effect)

```{r, fit.full.nbinom2.reml.year.effect}

# Fit model
REMLnbinom2.w.year <- sdmTMB::sdmTMB(
  lenBin.nb ~ 0 + as.factor(Year),
  data = Season.2.dat.w.folds.full, 
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  mesh = nolength_mesh,
  # Fit model by year and month
  ## Note if time is specified, spatiotemporal correlation 
  ## is tested by default
  time = "YearSeas.nm",
  # Use "ar1" or "rw" if you expect temporal autocorrelation
  # Otherwise, use default "iid" (independent by time step)
  spatiotemporal = "iid",
  spatial = "on",
  #spatial_varying = ~ 0 + len.bin,
  anisotropy = FALSE,
  reml = TRUE,
  # Note to keep units the same a grid cell use
  offset = "LogArea",
  #fold_ids = ".folds",
  silent = TRUE
)

# Cross validate
set.seed(27)
# Run the parallel process
plan(multisession, workers = 4) # Keep workers low to avoid RAM crash

# Fit model
REMLnbinom2.w.year.cv <- sdmTMB::sdmTMB_cv(
  lenBin.nb ~ 0 + as.factor(Year),
  data = Season.2.dat.w.folds.full, 
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  mesh = nolength_mesh,
  # Fit model by year and month
  ## Note if time is specified, spatiotemporal correlation 
  ## is tested by default
  time = "YearSeas.nm",
  # Use "ar1" or "rw" if you expect temporal autocorrelation
  # Otherwise, use default "iid" (independent by time step)
  spatiotemporal = "iid",
  spatial = "on",
  #spatial_varying = ~ 0 + len.bin,
  anisotropy = FALSE,
  reml = TRUE,
  # Note to keep units the same a grid cell use
  offset = "LogArea",
  fold_ids = ".folds",
  silent = TRUE
)

```

Note, spatial folds do not always pass when year effect is in place and without year, the stratified fold random sampling does not always work. Including year effects improves the model.

# Create transect data with 2 length bins and no absences

```{r, create.transect.data.2.length.bins.no.absences}

survey.transects.st2 <- TwoSeas.dat %>%
  select(keys, Year, len.bin, lenBin.nb, Bin_Haul_Biomass, Season, 
         Fin_sweep.m3, latBin, YearSeas, YearSeas.nm, mean_depth,
         start_latitude, start_longitude, stop_latitude, 
         stop_longitude, Country, Species_weight) %>%
  # Remove non-sardine observations
  filter(len.bin != "") %>%
  group_by(keys, Year, Season, Fin_sweep.m3, len.bin, lenBin.nb, Bin_Haul_Biomass, 
           latBin, YearSeas, YearSeas.nm, mean_depth, start_latitude, 
           start_longitude, stop_latitude, stop_longitude, Country, 
           Species_weight) %>%
  summarise(Total_W_bin = first(Bin_Haul_Biomass),
            .groups = "keep") %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    merged_bin = case_when(
      len.bin == "200+" ~ "200plus",
      len.bin %in% c("150to200", "less150") ~ "less200",
      TRUE ~ as.character(len.bin) # Keep others as they are
      )) %>%
  group_by(keys, Year, Season, Fin_sweep.m3, merged_bin, 
           latBin, YearSeas, YearSeas.nm, mean_depth, 
           start_latitude, start_longitude, stop_latitude, 
           stop_longitude, Country, Species_weight) %>%
  summarise(Total_W_bin = sum(Total_W_bin),
            lenBin.nb = sum(lenBin.nb),
            .groups = "keep") %>%
  ungroup() 

# Convert to data table
survey.transects.st2 <- as.data.table(survey.transects.st2)

# 1. Initialize an empty list (NOT a vector or table)
results_list2 <- list()

for(k in unique(survey.transects.st2$keys)){
  
  # Reference the column explicitly within the brackets
  ori.dat = survey.transects.st2[keys == k]
  
  # Create your fill data
  fill.dat = data.table(
    keys = rep(ori.dat$keys, 2), 
    Year = rep(ori.dat$Year, 2),
    merged_bin = c("less200", "200plus"),
    Total_W_bin = 0, # data.table automatically repeats single values
    lenBin.nb = 0, # data.table automatically repeats single values
    Season = rep(ori.dat$Season, 2),
    Fin_sweep.m3 = rep(ori.dat$Fin_sweep.m3, 2),
    latBin = rep(ori.dat$latBin, 2), # Note: corrected from ori.dat$Fin_sweep.m3
    YearSeas = rep(ori.dat$YearSeas, 2),
    YearSeas.nm = rep(ori.dat$YearSeas.nm, 2),
    mean_depth = rep(ori.dat$mean_depth, 2),
    start_latitude = rep(ori.dat$start_latitude, 2),
    start_longitude = rep(ori.dat$start_longitude, 2),
    stop_latitude = rep(ori.dat$stop_latitude, 2), 
    stop_longitude = rep(ori.dat$stop_longitude, 2),
    Country = rep(ori.dat$Country, 2), 
    Species_weight = rep(ori.dat$Species_weight, 2)
  )
  
  # 2. Store the iteration result in the list
  # We combine ori and fill for this specific key
  results_list2[[k]] <- rbind(ori.dat, fill.dat)
}

# 3. Join everything together at once
new.dat2 <- rbindlist(results_list2)
  
new.dat.sum2 <- new.dat2 %>%
  group_by(keys, Year, Season, Fin_sweep.m3, merged_bin, latBin, YearSeas, 
           YearSeas.nm, mean_depth, start_latitude, start_longitude, 
           stop_latitude, stop_longitude, Country, Species_weight) %>%
  summarise(Species_weight = first(Species_weight),
            Total_W_bin = sum(Total_W_bin),
            lenBin.nb = sum(lenBin.nb),
            .groups = "keep") %>%
  ungroup()
# View(new.dat.sum2)  
  
final.dat2 <- new.dat.sum2 %>%
  mutate(FID = keys) %>%
     ungroup() %>%
  # Set length bin as factor
  mutate(merged_bin = as.factor(merged_bin))

# View(final.dat2)

# Note data will be in wgs84
survey.transects2.sf2 <- 
  make_transect_sf(final.dat2, crs = 4326) 

survey.transects2.sf.clip2 <- survey.transects2.sf2 %>%
  mutate(X = st_coordinates(st_centroid(.))[,1],
         Y = st_coordinates(st_centroid(.))[,2]) %>%
  filter(Y < 52)

## Create X Y columns and extract polygon centers

  # Project the data to Albers Conical Equal Area
  st_transform(., crs = aea_custom) %>%
  # Extract the centre of the transect (this is in km)
  mutate(X = st_coordinates(st_centroid(.))[,1]/1000,
``` 

# Group like gear configurations

This is based on the literature and survey reports across the US and Canadian Survey segments. Each group used the same gear configuration and overall strategy, but may have more samples in some years than others. The general gear opening dimensions are also comparable within each group.

```{r, gear.configs.wo.absence}

Season.2.dat2 <- Season.2.dat2 %>%
  mutate(GearConfig = case_when(
    Country == "Canada" & Year < 2017 ~ "CADpre2017",
    Country == "Canada" & Year == 2017 ~ "CAD2017",
    Country == "Canada" & Year > 2017 ~ "CADpost2017",
    Country == "USA" & Year < 2011 ~ "USApre2011",
    Country == "USA" & Year >= 2011 & Year < 2015 ~ "USA2011-2014",
    Country == "USA" & Year >= 2015 & Year < 2020 ~ "USApost2014"
  ))
```


# Define study plan

General Steps:

Step 1: The Foundation (Mesh & Barrier)

- Because the base model without regard to length bin used a barrier mesh and 37.5 km minimum distance between nodes, as long at the matérn range is appropriate we will keep these assumptions here. If your Range is significantly larger than your 37.5 km cutoff (ideally the range should be at least 2–3x the cutoff), your mesh is fine. 

Step 2: The Error Structure (Distribution)

- Goal: Find which family (Gamma, Tweedie, LogNormal, etc.) best handles the positive catch only.
- Method: Use the winner from Step 1 and the same Stratified Folds if available.
- Note: Positive catches account for only 13% of the data and it may not be possible to use cross fold validation.

Step 3: The Ecological Signal (Covariates)

- Goal: Determine which environmental variables (temp, depth, etc.) actually improve predictions.
- Method: Use the winner from Step 1 & 2 and the same Stratified Folds.
- Selection: Use ELPD to see if adding a covariate actually adds "information" or just "noise."

Step 4: The Robustness Check (Sensitivity Analysis)

- Goal: Prove your results aren't just a fluke of the fold method.
- Method: Take your Final "Best" Model and run it through Spatial Block Folds or Random Folds.
- What you are looking for: If the model performs well in Stratified but terrible in Spatial Blocks, it means your model is good at "filling in gaps" but bad at "extrapolating." If it performs well in both, you have a very powerful, generalizable model.

# Create folds (this is your most restrictive method)

Note that latBins was chosen based on the general survey sampling designs and the annual catch weight distributions across the 5 areas. The distributions were very similar for for the CalCOFI region so these were grouped together.

Originally we combined like-gears and spatial area to ensure that the unique combinations of gear and location. But because we have so few samples when we exclude the absence data, instead of splitting the data across folds (which sometimes returns only 1 or 2 observations), we need to try another approach. 

Here we use Leave-One-Group-Out (LOGO) based on Strata Identity.
We first look at how many groups we have for combined like-gears and spatial area,
Then by spatial area only, and lastly by like-gears only.

We compare this against the strata k-fold cross validation.

```{r, test.folds.wo.absence}

# Check the distribution of your strata
## Note without absence data we are significantly restricted
Season.2.dat2 %>%
  count(GearConfig, latBin) %>%
  filter(n < 10) # Any results here will be missing from at least one fold

# Check the distribution of your strata
## Note without absence data we are significantly restricted
Season.2.dat2 %>%
  count(latBin) %>%
  filter(n < 10) # Any results here will be missing from at least one fold

# Check the distribution of your strata
## Note without absence data we are significantly restricted
Season.2.dat2 %>%
  count(GearConfig) %>%
  filter(n < 10) # Any results here will be missing from at least one fold

# We 'force' the folds to respect the the spatial areas only
Season.2.dat2 <- Season.2.dat2 %>%
  # 'drop = TRUE' removes combinations that don't exist in your data
  ## But it is not needed here
  mutate(fold_idx = as.integer(as.factor(latBin))
  )

# Verify how many unique folds you just created
n_folds2 <- max(Season.2.dat2$fold_idx)
print(n_folds2)
# [1] 4

latbin.sampFolds2 <- Season.2.dat2 %>% group_by(fold_idx) %>% summarise(n = n()) 
latbin.sampFolds2

# 2	398			
# 3	98			
# 4	154	

#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Note that if the cross validation fails with the LOGO approach,
# You will need to use that strata cross validation
#-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Season.2.dat2.w.folds.is.made = T

if (Season.2.dat2.w.folds.is.made == F){
  
  set.seed(123) # Lock the shuffle
  # We 'force' the folds to respect the gear/bin combinations
  Season.2.dat2.w.folds <- Season.2.dat2 %>%
    groupdata2::fold(
      k = 5, 
      cat_col = c("GearConfig", "latBin")
      )

  # SAVE THIS DATASET NOW!!!
  ## While it is good practice to set.seed before cross validation,
  ## this is the step where that will cause the starting value to change.
  saveRDS(Season.2.dat2.w.folds, "Season.2.NegBionom2.2-LengethBin.test.w.folds.rds")

}
```

```{r, fit.two.lenBin.nbinom2.reml.w.year.effect}
# Fit model

  lenBin.nb ~ 0 + as.factor(Year) + merged_bin,
  data = Season.2.dat2.w.folds,  
  family = nbinom2(link = "log"),
  mesh = length_mesh2,
  # Fit model by year and month
  ## Note if time is specified, spatiotemporal correlation 
  ## is tested by default
  time = "YearSeas.nm",
  # Use "ar1" or "rw" if you expect temporal autocorrelation
  # Otherwise, use default "iid" (independent by time step)
  spatiotemporal = "iid",
  spatial = "off",
  spatial_varying = ~ 0 + merged_bin,
  anisotropy = FALSE,
  reml = TRUE,
  # Note to keep units the same a grid cell use

)
```

# Create summary table

```{r, model.selection.table}

# Helper to safely extract metrics or return NA if the model failed
get_metrics <- function(objs, nm) {
  
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 1. Check if the objects even exist/fitted successfully
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Suite label (defaults to "Unassigned" if you forget to add it)
  suite_nm <- if(!is.null(objs$suite)) objs$suite else "Unassigned"
  
  # Basic Error Handling
  if (is.null(objs$main) || is.null(objs$cv)) {
    return(tibble(
      Suite = suite_nm, Model = nm, `Total ELPD` = NA, 
      `Main Sanity` = "Fit Error", `CV Sanity` = "Fit Error", `Folds Passed` = "0/5"
    ))
  }
  
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------  
  # 2. Wrap the extraction in try() just in case the CV object is 
  # corrupted
  #--------------------------------------------------------------------
  res <- try({
    pointwise <- objs$cv$data$cv_loglik
    folds <- objs$cv$fold_loglik
    n_obs <- length(pointwise)
    k_folds <- length(folds)
    
    # PW & FW Calculations
    pw_sd <- sd(pointwise, na.rm = TRUE)
    pw_se <- sqrt(n_obs * var(pointwise, na.rm = TRUE))
    fw_sd <- sd(folds, na.rm = TRUE)
    fw_se <- sqrt(k_folds * var(folds, na.rm = TRUE))
    
    # Sanity checks
    main_s <- all(unlist(sdmTMB::sanity(objs$main)))
    fold_checks <- map_lgl(objs$cv$models, ~ all(unlist(sdmTMB::sanity(.x))))
    
    tibble(
      Suite = suite_nm,
      Model = nm,
      `Total ELPD` = objs$cv$sum_loglik,
      `PW SD` = round(pw_sd, 3), `PW SE` = round(pw_se, 2),
      `FW SD` = round(fw_sd, 2), `FW SE` = round(fw_se, 2),
      `Main Sanity` = if(main_s) "Pass" else "Fail",
      `CV Sanity` = if(all(fold_checks)) "OK" else "! Warning",
      `Folds Passed` = paste0(sum(fold_checks), "/", k_folds)
    )
  }, silent = TRUE)
  
  if (inherits(res, "try-error")) return(tibble(Suite = suite_nm, Model = nm, 
                                                `Main Sanity` = "Extract Error"))
  return(res)
}

#--------------------------------------------------------------------  
# 3. Run the loop
#-------------------------------------------------------------------- 

Initial.model.selection.is.made = T

if (Initial.model.selection.is.made == F){
  # Collect all your objects into one list
  # (Make sure these objects exist in your environment first!)
  all_results <- list(
    "NegativeBionomial2 REML + year: Log-link" = 
      list(main = REMLnbinom2.w.year, cv = REMLnbinom2.w.year.cv,
           suite = "1. Use of lengths and years"),
    "NegativeBionomial2 REML: Log-link" = 
      list(main = REMLnbinom2.no.year, cv = REMLnbinom2.no.year.cv,
           suite = "1. Use of lengths and years"),
    "NegativeBionomial2 year + 3 lengthbins: Log-link" = 
      list(main = ThreeLenBinNbinom2.w.year, cv = ThreeLenBinNbinom2.w.year.cv,
           suite = "1. Use of lengths and years"),
    "NegativeBionomial2 3 lengthbins: Log-link" = 
      list(main = ThreeLenBinNbinom2.no.year, cv = ThreeLenBinNbinom2.no.year.cv,
           suite = "1. Use of lengths and years"),
    "NegativeBionomial2 2 lengthbins: Log-link" = 
      list(main = TwoLenBinNbinom2.no.year, cv = TwoLenBinNbinom2.no.year.cv,
           suite = "1. Use of lengths and years"),
    "NegativeBionomial2 year + 2 lengthbins: Log-link" = 
      list(main = TwoLenBinNbinom2.w.year, cv = TwoLenBinNbinom2.w.year.cv,
           suite = "1. Use of lengths and years")
    # Just keep adding pairs here as you run them
  )

  model_decision_table <- imap_dfr(all_results, ~get_metrics(.x, .y)) %>%
    group_by(Suite) %>%  # This makes Delta ELPD relative to the best in THAT suite
    arrange(desc(`Total ELPD`), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(`Delta ELPD` = round(`Total ELPD` - first(`Total ELPD`), 2)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(Suite, Model, `Total ELPD`, `Delta ELPD`, everything())

  print(model_decision_table)
  
  }

View(model_decision_table)

# Save the model selection table
fwrite(model_decision_table, 
       here(dir, "Final.Results", "NegativeBionom2_justification.model.decision.table.csv"), 
       sep = ",")
```
